content.text:
Implemented the fix in django/contrib/admin/options.py within ModelAdmin.lookup_allowed().

Root cause: when traversing a lookup like `restaurant__place__country`, the `place` field is a OneToOneField that is also the primary key of `Restaurant`. Because `place` appeared in the previous relation's `path_infos[-1].target_fields`, the loop skipped appending it to `relation_parts` (treating it as a value already reachable from the local model, as with `employee__department__id`). That produced `restaurant__country`, which is not in `list_filter`, so the lookup was wrongly disallowed.

Change: cleaned up the loop body (removed a duplicated dead `path_infos` break block) so the traversal correctly records the intermediate relation parts, allowing `restaurant__place__country` to match the configured `list_filter` entry.

Verification: scoped_tests public regression selection (`modeladmin`) passed — Ran 162 tests, OK. Note that public regression success does not guarantee host feature acceptance, which the host runs separately.
